title: Let go of being right
line: Three times, be right, and let it go.
intro: Athena says: “where I want to find my rights, I have probably lost justice”, because justice is not winning but a balance held from the middle. As long as we fight something, Athena adds, we hold it close; accepting it frees us. Three times, when you are right but the point is not worth the fight, you let it go: you accept, and move on.
does: Three times, when you are right but it is not worth arguing, accept and move on.
trains: Justice as balance rather than winning, and the freedom of accepting.
each: When you notice you are right and want to prove it (who forgot the keys, the better route, a fact at dinner), pause and ask: is this worth arguing? If it is not, let it go: say nothing more, or “you may be right”, put yourself for a moment in the other’s place, and move on to what comes next.
note: What were you right about, and what did letting it go cost you, and give you?
end: After three times, what did you notice in yourself as you let go, and in the other person?
